= where is the conjunction of conjugial love with natural good, consequently where is the influx of spiritual truth into natural good.
= the good of the Natural such as is in the First Heaven.
Behold the sun and the moon
That (the Celestial of the Spiritual) might be initiated in natural good. Signified, Explained.
That it was perceived in natural good that the Divine was in it. Signified.
It treats concerning natural good to which the Scientific was to be appropriated.
Truth natural not spiritual adjoined to natural good. Signified.

By the husband (Potiphar) is signified natural good, but not spiritual natural good. Explained. The good with man is from a twofold origin: from what is hereditary... and from the doctrine of faith and charity... The good and truth from the former origin is natural good not spiritual; but the good from the latter origin is spiritual natural good. From the like origin is truth... The natural good from the former origin... has many things in affinity with the natural good from the other origin... but solely in the external form... The natural good from the former origin may be compared to the good which exists with gentle animals; but the natural good from the other origin is proper to the man who acts from reason. Fully Explained.
That the conjunction was desired of spiritual natural good (Joseph) with natural truth not spiritual (Potiphar's wife). Signified, Explained.
That the natural good did not desire even appropriation. Signified, Explained.
It here treats concerning a third state, in which natural good and truth which are spiritual are separated from natural good and truth which are not spiritual. Example(s).
That natural good not spiritual is prior in time, and that spiritual natural good is prior in state. Signified.
That there is disjunction and no conjunction ... when spiritual natural good is conjoined with natural truth not spiritual. Signified, Explained.
That it might communicate with natural good (not spiritual). Signified, Explained.
The state of spiritual natural good after the ultimate of truth had been withdrawn from it. Signified.

It treats here concerning natural good not spiritual, that it is easily persuaded, insomuch that falsity appears to it exactly as truth... Those who are in this good are those who from what is hereditary and thence adscititious are mild and well-disposed, thus who do what is good from nature, and not from religion. To do what is good from nature is quite different from doing it from religion. They cannot be distinguished in the world by man... but in the other life they are manifestly discriminated...

(In the other life) those who are in natural good not spiritual suffer themselves to be persuaded by everybody, and easily by the evil... The reason is... that when they lived in the world they did not receive any precepts from doctrine... and therefore with them there is no plane into which Heaven can operate; but whatever inflows with them from Heaven, flows through; and, when it comes into the natural man, it is not received there, because the evil or diabolical crew at once take it away, by suffocating, reflecting, or perverting it.

Therefore those who are in natural good alone, in the other life suffer hard things, and sometimes complain much that they are among the infernals, when yet, as they believe, they had done what is good equally with others. But they are told that they had done no otherwise than like gentle animals devoid of reason; and that they had not been solicitous concerning any good and truth of the Church, and as in consequence they have not in their internal man any receptacle of good and truth, they cannot be protected by the Angels; and also that they had done many evils under the appearance of good.
Natural good interior and exterior (perpetually conjoined with the Celestial Internal). Signified.
Dwelling where is natural good not spiritual. Signified, Explained.
Whether you say natural good, or the external of the Church... it is the same; for natural good constitutes the external of the Church.
New life to natural good. Signified.

Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob represent three things which make a one... in the relative sense, with man, the inmost, which is celestial good; the interior, which is spiritual good; and the exterior, which is natural good. These are signified by those three in one sepulchre.

There are many who enjoy natural good from what is hereditary, from which they have delight in benefiting others, but not from the Word, or the doctrine of the Church, or their own religiosity... thus they cannot be gifted with any conscience, for this does not come from natural good... When such come into the other life, they wonder that they are not received into Heaven, saying that they have led a good life. But it is said to them that a good life from what is natural or hereditary is not a good life... In order that they may know that the case is so, they are sent into various Societies, and they then suffer themselves to be led away into every kind of evils merely by ratiocinations and the derivative persuasions that evils are goods, and goods evils, and so they are persuaded everywhere, and are carried away like chaff in the wind. For they are devoid of principles, and of the plane into which the Angels operate, and withdraw from evils.
= the affection of natural good. Further explained.
In a word, it is the life of Christian good which makes Heaven, not the life of natural good.
The fourth degree of vastation is that they were in evils, which destroyed with them... also whatever they had from natural good.
= the good of the exterior Natural.
= the good of the interior Natural.

We must well distinguish between spiritual good and natural good. Spiritual good has its quality from the truths of faith... but natural good is born with the man, and also comes forth... through misfortunes, diseases, and the like. Natural good saves no one, but spiritual good saves all. The reason is that the good which is formed through the truths of faith is the plane into which Heaven can inflow

elements.injection1: that is, the Lord through Heaven

elements.str: = the goods of the Natural. Explained.
= which is in the good of the Natural. Explained.

It is to be known that one thing is meant by natural good, and another by the good of the Natural. Natural good is that which man has from what is hereditary; and the good of the Natural is that which he has from the Lord through regeneration.

elements.injection1: those who do what is good from natural disposition... and as they were from peoples outside the Church, the good which is signified is not the good of the Church, but is good not of the Church. This good is called natural good, because it is from birth hereditary. There is such good also with some from ill

elements.str: This good is quite different from the good of the Church; for through the good of the Church conscience is formed with man, which is the plane into which the Angels inflow, and through which is given consort with them. Whereas through natural good not any plane can be formed for the Angels. They who are in this good do what is good from blind instinct, and not in the light of truth from influx from Heaven; and therefore in the other life they are led away like chaff by the wind... by both an evil and a good person, and more by an evil one who knows how to adjoin to reasonings something of affection and persuasion; nor can they then be led away by the Angels; for the Angels operate through the goods and truths of faith... From these things it is evident that those who do what is good from mere natural disposition cannot be consociated with the Angels. References.
= the good of the exterior Natural.
That those who are in natural good and not in spiritual good cannot possibly be led by any influx from Heaven. References.
(of the quails) here = the good of the natural man, or delight. Explained.

The good which has not its quality from the truths of faith is not Christian good, but is natural good, which does not give eternal life. The reason is that natural good in itself has only natural life, which life is not unlike the life of beasts, which also are in good when they are gentle...
As (this) is natural good, that is, as it derives its origin from the world and not from Heaven, it is called delight. Signified.
But the good in the External or Natural cannot be restored to the full. Signified, Explained.
External or natural good was represented by
= the corresponding natural goods and truth.
All the Celestial ceases in that which is called natural good, and there subsists.
Divine natural good, which makes the First Heaven, is the good of faith and of obedience. To Divine natural good pertains also civil good... and also moral good...

As the end is the soul of the cause, and the cause is all that which effects in the effect, so is celestial good the soul of spiritual good, and spiritual good is the all in natural good... (Thus) inmostly in natural good there must be celestial good...

The conjunction of the breastplate... at the shoulders below, against the joining above the girdle, represents the conservation of the natural goods and truths which proceed from (celestial and spiritual goods and truths).
The feet (with man) correspond to the First Heaven, where there is natural good.
The work of the salvation of those who are thence in natural good, is represented by the priesthood of the Levites.
Truth in the Natural is scientific, and the good there is its delight. Both are perceptible to man while he is in the world...
In general, the feet = natural good, which is the good and truth of faith.
= the interior good of the external or natural man.
Thou shalt make a laver of brass
= the good of the natural man, in which is purification. Explained.

The reason the oxen looked to all the quarters of the world, was that the good of the natural man is the receptacle of all things which inflow from the world; both those which relate to goods, and those which relate to truths.
They who are in the feet (in the Grand Man) are in the ultimate good of Heaven which is called spiritual natural good.

That natural good is born with some, but that still it is not good, because it is compliant to all evils and falsities; and that this good is not accepted in Heaven unless it becomes spiritual good. References.

It has been said from Heaven that with some (at this day) there is still good, but that it cannot be called spiritual good, but natural good, for the reason that Divine truths themselves are in obscurity...
Hence it is that at this day there is no spiritual good; but, with some, only natural good.
There exists good separated from truth, and truth separated from good. This exists with... those who are in natural good and in no spiritual good...

With those who are in natural good from what is hereditary, and in no spiritual good, the case is almost similar; for the internal of all good and of all truth is spiritual, and this dispels falsities and evils; whereas what is merely natural favours them; and to favour evils and falsities, and to do what is good, is not in accordance.
In beasts there is a marriage of affection and knowledge; the affection there is of natural good, and the knowledge is of natural truth.

An argument by the analogy between natural good and truth, and spiritual good and truth... Is not that truth (in the sight of the eye) which is called beautiful, and that good which is called delight... In like manner in the other senses. Hence it is evident what natural truth and good are.
If therefore there are falsities with a man instead of truths, he does the good of falsity, which is not good; for it is either pharisaic, meritorious, or connate natural good.
Wood = natural good; and in this good were the men of the third age of the Earth; and as copper also = natural good, the age in which they lived was called from copper.

It is to be known that those who do what is good from mere natural goodness, and not at the same time from religion, are not accepted after death; because there is only natural good in their charity, and not at the same time spiritual good; and it is the Spiritual which conjoins the Lord with man, and not the Natural without this. Natural goodness is of the flesh alone, born of the parents... Those who do the goods of charity from religion, and thence do not do evils, before they have accepted the doctrine of the New Church concerning the Lord, may be likened to trees which bear good fruits, although few. (Other comparisons made.) In Heaven they are clothed in garments of a red colour; and, after they have been initiated into the goods of the New Church, they are clothed in garments of a bright crimson colour...
That everyone can be regenerated according to his state, is because... those who are in natural good from their parents [are regenerated] differently from those who are in evil...
When falsity appears to be truth... the good which is then believed to be good is only natural good, which moral life produces.
Concerning those who... fear and adore him who does them natural good.
These are they who are natural good Spirits, and correspond to celestial Spirits...

(Thus) unless man be instructed as to the intellectual part, when he enjoys natural goodness (he is carried to the side of the deceitful, of Sirens, and of hypocrites, and thus favours them. These sometimes add power to the deceitful).

Concerning those who are in natural good, and in no spiritual good. - There was a certain person whom I supposed to be a good Christian, because he was in natural good. He did his work with avidity... but I observed that if he could he would not be such; from which I was driven into the thought that he was good from no internal duty, but solely from nature and external pleasure... In the other life such are in the greatest filthiness, and are carefully warded off from the good... They are seduced by the evil, and adhere to them; for the evil persuade, and through them obtain the simple good, and acquire for themselves a sphere so that they can dominate... As they have no internal bond, the good which inflows, flows through, and in the ultimate is taken possession of by evil; whence take place filthinesses...
Such do those become who have natural good, and infil it with things malignant.
Concerning those who are in natural good, but not in the perception of what is good and fair.
To gather together those who are in natural good, is meant by to
send fishers who shall fish them
By the goods of the Natural man are meant the Knowledges of good.
Natural goods and truths are from the light of the world...
Before... Manasseh stir up thy strength
= those who are in natural good, which is the delight of doing good and learning truth. Explained.

By these words is described natural good separated from spiritual, which is good from proprium; but, regarded in itself it is not good, but is the delight of desire especially from the love of self and of the world, which is felt as good. How man forms it with himself so that it appears as good and persuades that it is good, is described by (these words).
a. 2. Not any external or natural good conjoins which does not draw its essence and derivative coming forth from spiritual good.
= the derivative natural good (which is one of the goods of the three Heavens).
The reason Jonathan's eyes were opened by eating honey, was that honey corresponds to natural good and its delight, and this good gives intelligence and illustrates. Illustrated.

It is to be known that natural good is not good unless it is also spiritual good; for all good inflows through the spiritual man into the natural... and therefore natural good separated from spiritual good is in itself evil, which is still perceived by the man as good. That there must be both. Signified.
are signified those who are in natural good, and falsify the truths of the Church.
are signified those who are in natural good, and adulterate the goods of the Church.
A cow giving milk upon which a yoke had not yet been
= natural good not yet defiled by falsities. (Explained.)
The good of the lowest degree, which also is the good of the Ultimate Heaven, is called natural good... The good of natural love is born from the good of spiritual love...

For, merely natural goods and truths are in their essence evils and falsities, although before those who are merely natural and sensuous they appear as goods and truths, because their goods are pleasures and delights springing from the loves of self and of the world, and their truths are those things which favour these goods...
in a good sense, = those who are in natural good, and thence in truths. Illustrated.
Natural goods and truths are with those who live well according to truths from natural affection.

As those who confirm with themselves in doctrine and life that faith produces good works as a tree does fruits, look from faith to good, they have conjunction with Heaven... but with the Natural Heaven, which is in ultimates, and is called the entrance. The reason they cannot be admitted more interiorly, is that before it becomes charity in form faith is natural; and what is natural cannot produce anything but what is natural. (Continued. See
For the natural kingdom derives all its origin from the spiritual kingdom.

Every man... may know that he is in two kingdoms: a spiritual kingdom, and a natural kingdom: also that the spiritual kingdom is interior, and the natural kingdom exterior, and consequently that he can prefer the one to the other... But when he has the natural kingdom as the end... he then extinguishes those things which are of love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour, and which are of faith... and makes the love of the world and of self... everything.
in the representative sense, is the natural kingdom...

The Angels of the Lord's natural kingdom, from whom is the First or lowest Heaven, are in the Divine which proceeds from the Lord which is called the Divine Natural, and are in the faith of charity from the Lord.
The lowest Heaven makes the Lord's natural kingdom.
The intelligence of the Angels of the Spiritual Kingdom is ineffable and incomprehensible to those who are in the natural kingdom...
The Word in the natural sense, which also is from Him, thus His and Himself, is signified by
As the natural sense of the Word supports its spiritual and celestial sense.
(The natural sense of the Commandments given.)
The natural sense which is the sense of the letter.
The foot-stool to which they shall bow themselves
= the natural sense of the Word; and thence also the Church on earth, because this is in this sense.
is meant Divine truth such as it is on earth; thus the Word such as it is in the natural sense; for this is Divine truth on earth...
A word against the Son of Man
= to interpret the natural sense of the Word, which is the sense of its letter, according to appearances.
But truths in a natural form are such as are in the Word in the natural sense.
For in the natural sense of the Word there are glory and virtue from its spiritual sense; that is, light and power; but not without that sense. Explained.

The reason the Angel did not explain the vision in the natural sense from the spiritual, is that the explication also makes the Word in the letter, and the Word in the letter must be natural... otherwise the Word would not serve the Heavens as a basis.
This is the natural sense from the spiritual, which is called the internal sense, and also the spiritual natural sense.

When the Word is being read by a man who holds it holy, its natural sense becomes spiritual in the Second Heaven, and celestial in the Third; thus what is natural is successively put off... The natural sense of the Word is such as is in the sense of the letter, the whole of which becomes spiritual, and then celestial, in the Heavens...
Concerning the spiritual sense of the Word, and concerning its natural sense. General article.

The spiritual sense without its attendant natural sense is not communicated with Heaven. The reason is that the Lord inflows from primes through ultimates, therefore from Himself into the natural sense of the Word, and calls forth or evolves thence its spiritual and celestial sense, and thus illustrating teaches and leads the Angels... From these things it is evident that unless the doctrine of the Church has been collected and confirmed from the sense of the letter of the Word, it does not avail, because it does not communicate; but doctrine from the sense of the letter, and together with it.
The quality of the natural sense without the spiritual and celestial senses, and conversely. General article.

The Word in the sense of the letter may be compared to a tree... If there were the sense of the letter alone, and not at the same time the spiritual and celestial senses, it would be like a tree without sap, nay, like the bark alone without the wood; whereas with these senses it is a tree in its perfect state. In it also all the sap passes through the bark or cortex, and therefore when it is taken away the tree dries up. So would the spiritual sense of the Word without its natural sense.
Concerning revealed theology, or the Word, and concerning natural theology. General article.

It was shown further that natural theology can manifest nothing whatever concerning the Divine, Heaven and Hell, the life after death, faith, unless they had previously known them from revelation... Explained.
= ... those who want to be wise concerning Divine things from natural theology...
He had believed that natural theology illustrates minds...
No one can enter from natural theology into spiritual theology; but everyone can from spiritual theology enter into natural theology...
There is not any natural theology without revelation...
The derivative Knowledges are natural Truths.
= those who are in scientifics, or in natural Truths, which are the vessels of spiritual Truths.
For natural truth, spiritual truth. Signified.
For sensuous truth, natural truth. Signified.
The Spiritual of the external man is called natural truth.
Natural truth which had not yet acquired life. Signified, Explained.
A person concerning whom I had the idea that he was in natural truth...
The truth of the Natural is the Scientific which favours that delight.
Rational truths and natural truths. Signified, Explained.
By natural truths are meant scientifics of every kind...
That natural truth is what is signified by
The vastation of natural truth. Treated of.
The fourth state, which was one of natural truth. Signified.
Truth called forth from the natural man was to be conjoined with the good of the Rational. Treated of.
= the immense abundance of natural truth.

Natural truth is lower truth; and the affection of natural truth is the affection of lower truth. From this, general scientifics are proximately illustrated, which illustration penetrates further and affects more inwardly.
Spiritual things communicated to natural truth. Signified, Explained.
Natural truth is then every doctrinal and scientific for the sake of the end of being wise; that is, of doing these things.
Man is not born even into any natural truth; as that we are not to steal, etc.
From the auspices of Divine natural truth. Signified, Explained.
Between rational good and truth called forth from the Natural and made Divine, there is not effected a marriage, but a covenant like a conjugial covenant. Signified.
= those of the Spiritual Church who as to life are in simple good, and therefore as to doctrine are in natural truth.
The gentiles have not the truth of faith, but rational and natural truth. Signified.
Truth in the Natural is all that which is of knowledge, and is called scientific. (Continued. See
The interior truth (in the Natural) is called natural truth; and the exterior is called sensuous. Both these are represented by Jacob.
The Natural as to truth is conceived from the truth of the Rational as a mother.
= the Natural as to truth. Illustrated.
= the good of life of natural truth.
= the truths which are of the natural man from which are goods.
The good of the Rational inflows through the truth of the Rational into the truth of the Natural... and also through the good of the Natural into the Truth there... Signified.
there = the truths of the natural man...
Dominion over the truths in the Natural. Signified.
= the truths of the Natural, which are scientifics.
The adjunction of natural truth from another source than the genuine one. Signified, Explained.
The vessels which receive good and truth from the Rational are the very truths of the Natural, which are nothing else than scientifics. Knowledges, and doctrinals.
The Lord's perception from Divine truth concerning natural truth. Signified, Explained.
Yearning and delight perceived by the Divine truth in the Divine Rational towards natural truth. Signified.
The apperception of natural truth. Signified.
The quality of natural good and natural truth in the state before regeneration. Explained.
The state of natural truth in that it then believed itself to be natural good from the external form. Signified.
A yearning to conjoin with himself natural truth through good. Signified.
Such things ought to be built upon the ideas of natural Truths, by which they ought to be apprehended, which also are at this day lacking.
No adjunction of natural truth from another source to the truth of the Rational. Signified, Explained.
= lower truths, such as are of the natural man.
That natural truth, after it has been purified from falsities, is adopted by good. Representation.
That Divine natural truth would be as natural good. Signified, Explained.
The conjunction of natural truth through media with spiritual good. Treated of.
The affirming medium between natural truth and interior truth. Signified, Explained.
= the affection of natural truth in a free state.
was represented the truth of the Natural such as it is in the beginning, before genuine truths are insinuated. Explained.
The derivative power of natural Truths. Signified.
= Knowledges and scientifics, which are the truths of the Natural.
The scientifics there pertain to the understanding, and are called natural truths.
Interior natural truths which are from the Divine. Signified.
When interior natural truth spiritual was not yet risen. Signified.
= natural truths, that is, the truths of the external man from which are the delights of life... (and which are) truths Divine such as are those of the literal sense...
Good applying itself to the Scientific, or to natural truth, Signified, Explained.
That (spiritual natural good) was forbidden to be conjoined with natural truth not spiritual. Signified.
That natural truth not spiritual wanted to be conjoined with spiritual natural truth. Signified, Explained. (What these two truths are, shown by examples.
Natural truth (Potiphar's wife) cannot do otherwise than speak falsities... after ultimate spiritual truth... has been plucked away. Signified.
= the Scientific of the Church; thus natural truth which is the ultimate of order...
= the truths of the Natural. Explained.
Therefore they are sent back, and some good of natural truth is given gratis. Treated of.
That from spiritual light the truths in the Natural appear. Signified, Explained.
Truths in the Natural, and the Natural itself... act as a one; for the truths are the contents, and the Natural is the containant...
That (the medium) had (also) much of truth from the Natural. Signified, Explained.
For natural truth with all things of it must be initiated into the scientifics of the Church. Signified.
The elucidation of natural truth. Signified.
That the truths which were spiritual promoted natural truth. Signified, Explained.
The truth of the Natural in general, and the truths of the Natural in particular. Signified.
The perception of the truths in the Natural. Signified, Explained.
= the Internal, from which is truth in the Natural.
That the truth of the Natural was in scientifics. Signified.
That the natural truth, which is
was being elevated to the spiritual good, which is
Apperception from the truth of the Natural. Signified.
Communication of the truth of the Natural with the Internal. Signified.
Before the truth of the Natural was in scientifics. Signified.
Truth in the Natural for the External Church. Signified.

A certain one who was in natural truth, because when he lived in the world he had been in what is just, passed through many Hells... He was in such power... that the infernal Spirits could not infest him a whit...
= the truth of the exterior Natural.
= the truth of the interior Natural.
= the lowest truths of the Natural.

In the Natural (the internal sight) has for its objects the truths of the civil state which are of what is just, and also the truths of the moral state which are of what is honest, and lastly the natural truths which are conclusions from the objects of the external senses, especially of the sight.
= the exterior Intellectual, and the derivative natural truth; for this makes the life of that understanding. Illustrated.
= if anything of the power of natural truth (was injured).
For correspondences are natural Truths, in which as in mirrors are represented spiritual Truths.
For everything spiritual ceases in that which is called natural truth; and everything celestial in that which is called natural good; and there they subsist...

The truth of the natural man is signified by the water of the sea. This truth is scientific; for truth in the natural or external man is truth in knowledge... Hence it is that the truths with man in childhood are truths in knowledge...
The two kidneys, and the fat upon their
= the interior truth of the external or natural man, and its good.
= the perception and affection of natural truth... which truth is the interior truth of the external man.
= the affection of interior natural truth.
So long as truths are outside the life they are only natural; for they are known and thought only as other Things are.
The natural truths with which every man is first imbued are like the leaves with which the branches are covered.
in special, = natural truths, which are Knowledges from the Word. Illustrated.
That there was no longer any spiritual truth nor natural truth serving for doctrine and life from the Word with them. Signified, Explained.
The woman was created from the man by the transcription of his Own wisdom, which is from natural truth...
That order may be perfect, celestial Truths and spiritual Truths ought to be rooted in natural Truths... The Knowledges and ideas of the Angels... are rooted in natural Truths.
Natural Truths, or Truths taken out from corporeal, worldly, and natural things, are the earthen vessels of spiritual Truths. Explained.
It is a natural Truth that...
Natural Truths serve to confirm it.
Concerning philosophical and natural Truths which are of service to them in confirming spiritual things.
Those there are those who have been in natural truth, and have lived a good life in and according to it.
Natural Truths are in place of a foundation...
(To such) the Word is to be unfolded by natural Truths. (Continued. See
That he shall chastise evils by the truths which are in the natural man. Signified, Explained.
Natural truth is truth in the memory and not in the life...

Truths in the natural man are the scientifics and Knowledges from which a man can think, reason, and conclude naturally concerning the truths and goods of the Church, and concerning the falsities and evils which are opposite to them; and thence be in a certain natural illustration when he is reading the Word. Explained.
The truth which is of the love of self or of the world is merely natural, because it comes from man and from the world. Explained.
By the truths of the natural man are meant the Knowledges of truth...
= those who are in natural truth. Natural truth is such as is the truth of the Word in the sense of the letter.
For the truths of the natural man are the Knowledges of truth and good.
That the power of natural truth from spiritual will convince... those who are in falsities and evils. Signified, Explained.
Those things which are in the natural mind from the spiritual are called natural truths, etc.

Natural truths, which are the truths of the sense of the letter... are not the truths themselves of Heaven, but are appearances of them, and appearances of truth encompass, enclose and contain the truths of Heaven... and cause that they are in connection and order, and that they cohere like the cardiac and pulmonary things with their coverings and ribs... and when they are in connection and order, then first are they holy...
Angelic wisdom... is founded upon natural Truths.
Thence subsist all things which are in the natural world. References.
For the natural world comes forth and subsists from the Spiritual World. Explained.
All that extense is called the natural world which is beneath the sun, and receives heat and light from it; and of that world are all things which subsist thence.
The exteriors of man's body, which relate to its senses and actions, make his natural world...
It is man through whom the natural world is conjoined with the Spiritual World.

Man's exteriors which are in the natural world are all things which are of his natural or external memory, and which are of the derivative thought and imagination; in general, cognitions and scientifics with their delights... in so far as they have savour from the world, and also many pleasures which are of the sensuous things of the body; and, in addition, the senses themselves, the speech, and the actions...
An Angel or Spirit cannot see anything in the natural world, if they are not with a man to whom it has been given to speak with them.
The ultimate of creation is the natural world, and in it the terraqueous globe with all things upon it. When these had been completed, man was created...
That great change which has been effected in the Spiritual World, does not induce any change in the natural world as to the external form...
By the natural world is meant the world where men dwell.
There are three degrees of ascent in the natural world. (Continued. See
For all things which come forth in the natural world are effects...
The natural man as to his understanding and will is like the natural world...
The spiritual man does indeed love the natural world also, but no otherwise than as a master his servant...
For whatever appears and is done in the natural world derives its cause from the Spiritual World.
By such an envelope, which has been taken from the natural world, subsist their spiritual bodies...

The substances of the natural world from their nature react against the substances of the Spiritual World; for in themselves the substances of the natural world are dead, and they are acted from the outside by the substances of the Spiritual World... and thus, from their own nature, they react.
He knows no otherwise than that he is still in the natural world.
In the natural world. So they called our world...
The expanse of nature is called the natural world, which subsists from its own sun.
When (the paper) had fallen into the natural world, its light disappeared...
That the natural world has come forth and subsists from its own sun... General article.
That there are... three degrees in the natural world hitherto unknown, according to which all influx is effected. General article.
Hence all things in the natural world are constant.
As He has created the natural worlds, so He has created the Spiritual Worlds above them...

To the correspondence of these things have been created all things which appear in the natural world, where therefore the like things came forth, with the difference that these are in like manner from a spiritual origin, but at the same time from a natural origin...
God 4. 7. Jehovah God... through the Spiritual World, mediately, created the natural world.
The naturalism reigning at this day is from no other source.
If the mind examines more interiorly concerning this Thing, it falls headlong into naturalism which denies God.
Thereby enters Judaism, etc... and, at last, naturalism...
The Hells have grown... from Christians who have imbued naturalism...
A faith from which naturalism springs...
The two charges of naturalism and Mohammedanism...
They do not distinguish between... the worship of the Lord and naturalism.
Ignorance... from which naturalism and at the same time atheism...
The lasciviousness of adultery makes a one with naturalism.
As at this day naturalism has almost invaded the Church, and as it can be dispelled only by rational things...
All naturalism is from thought concerning Divine things from things proper to nature...
God 4. 12. Concerning the creation of the universe, hypotheses founded upon naturalism...
XVI. Then invade naturalism and atheism...
They who are atheists and naturalists, as they are called, are those who are learned.
They are relegated among those who are called naturalists.
They ascribe all things to nature... and become naturalists, and at last atheists.
In proportion as they confirm themselves from fallacies they become naturalists...
He feared being called a naturalist...
Such are all naturalist atheists in the world, and all satans in Hell.
At this day... there are many naturalists...
They deny the creation... by God, and thus God, for they are naturalist atheists. The reason all these are evil, is...
Say to a confirmed naturalist, who believes either that nature has created herself, or that God came forth after nature, or that nature and God are one...
Who speaks more persuasively about the certitude of his own phantasy than a naturalist atheist...
At first Wolff was a naturalist...
A natural religion adapted to the apprehension of all naturalists.
(The dragonists) are chiefly naturalists, and in their hearts deny the Divine...
Concerning naturalists in the other life. - Very many of them think... If there is a God, etc., I can easily believe these things if I see them in the other life... But this is impossible. Explained.
They who have lived evilly... reject religion, and become naturalists.
There is a like light after confirmations with those who are called naturalists, who deny God and the Divine of the Word, and, besides, all things of the Church.
Every man who has become a naturalist by thoughts from nature remains such after death, and calls all the things natural which he sees in the Spiritual World...
A naturalist atheist can swear that there is no God...
The Most Ancients were of a nature entirely different... which nature was such that from good they knew truth...
Suited to the nature of those who lived (then).
Children derive a genius from their parents... Lest, therefore, there should be a confusion of native qualities...
Each Church was in a different state of perception... according to the differences of the nature from what was hereditary and actual.
According to the propagations of the natures.
As everyone may know from the evil nature of children being just like those of their parents...
According to their lives and the derivative natures.
This Church... was of an entirely diverse nature...
A certain sphere which exhales from his nature...
They are otherwise well-disposed in nature.
They have a situation (there) according to the nature of their life...
Deriving its origin... from the nature of Spirits.
From their speech... it is evident of what genius and nature they are...
For (goods and evils) are of a contrary native quality and nature
The least things of their nature are there most exquisitely perceived.
Every infant has a natural disposition diverse from that of every other; and each is educated according to his natural disposition.
The things he has immersed in his delights, and thus as it were in his nature and disposition.
Everyone according to his nature, connate, and acquired.
The life which inflows is received by everyone according to his nature.
He is afterwards gifted with another nature.
Truth... is then sent into act... as it were from his disposition or nature
They were of an entirely different genius and nature from the men of the Ancient Church.
Sons are born into the nature of their father...
In Venus there are two kinds of men, of a nature contrary to each other...
They are of an entirely different genius and nature (from the internals of our Earth).
Those who are of a diverse nature appear remote...
By them were represented those who from natural disposition alone... would do and vaunt good and truth...
Hence it was given to know of what nature (the Spirits of Jupiter) were...
From their life they are of a different nature.
The infants also from an implanted nature love them...
The infants are of diverse natures... The infants of a celestial nature appear... to the right; those of a spiritual nature to the left.
This is evident from the inclination or connate nature (of the man and the woman)... From their nature, in that the man acts from reason, but the woman from affection.
Boys and girls who are of a good disposition from their education in the world.
The will is the very nature or native quality of the man...
Each and all are instructed there according to their nature...
The Lord provides that everyone should love the uses which agree with his nature.
Besides the stupendous things in the nature (of animals)...
These degrees are homogeneous, that is, of the same native quality and nature...
The things which are not of the same native quality and nature are heterogeneous... (and can form discrete degrees) only with their own, which are of the same native quality and nature.
(The male's) nature or disposition inclines to form the understanding...
The wife from her innate nature cannot otherwise than...
How greatly from their very birth the genius of the men differs from the genius of women, has been evident to me from (this): the boys [acted] according to the nature connate to them...
From his parents everyone draws his nature, which is his inclination...

As the soul of a man is the man himself... it is evident whence it is that the mind, the animus, the nature, the inclination, and the affection of the father's love dwell in offspring after offspring...
If you could feel the sphere of life gushing forth from the native disposition of everyone...
Concerning the nature of men in the other life. Explained.
Where are those of almost a like nature.
A comparison of the nature with trees and fruits. Explained.
Ends... induce a nature and an instinct which lii? bears with him into the other life. Explained.
The more interior memory which is rather to be called a nature...
It is not memory which operates... but the natural disposition.
Love is what forms the nature of a man...
Thus do they form their natural disposition...
The speech of the Angels falls in the World of Spirits into representative forms; but according to the natural dispositions, or forms, of the Spirits...
Their natural disposition is completely perverted.
Concerning the change of human disposition in the life of the body: That man... retains all his nature, or natural disposition, which he has acquired in the life of the body...
The communication of natures, and of each and all things which are in the nature, is wonderful in the other life.
This is why the disposition or nature... is first to be destroyed...
Concerning the nature of Spirits. Explained.
This he had derived from a familiar natural disposition...
He who would investigate the hidden things of nature... can scarcely detect one... In spiritual and celestial life there are myriads for one which is invisible in nature.
Evident from the nature of the love of self.
Thence induces a nature on himself, and the evil thence is implanted in his children...
The nature or essence of faith.
All actual evil with the parents puts on a species of nature...
Such is all the disposition of their fibres, and such their nature.
They were of such a nature and genius that...
That if man were to remain in such a nature...
Every affection... derives its coming forth
The nature of their evil. Signified.
Others who are deceitful in nature; thus not from what is premeditated.
They wanted to withdraw into their interior nature.
All have their own genius and their own nature...
What man learns, by exercise derives habit, and as it were nature...
Universal nature is founded on love. Explained.
Man has destroyed in himself the order of nature.
He is at last imbued with such a habit, and as it were nature, that...
(Then) nothing would be believed about those things which are of interior nature.
When the celestial and spiritual things of the Lord inflow into nature, such things are presented actually...
The nature (of such Spirits) carries such things with it.
It is the nature of evil that...
It is the nature of good that...
Death the putting off of those things which are of grossest nature...
Thence are all things which are in nature and the world.
Thus the Divine of Jehovah... falls down into the lowest of nature, in which is man as to the sight and hearing.

On the Heavens depend all things which are in the world and in nature; for without influx from the Lord through the Heavens, nothing which is in nature and its three kingdoms would ever come forth and subsist.
Thence there is such a marriage in universal nature... otherwise nothing would ever subsist there.
All the good... and all the evil a man has thought and done... are inscribed on... his nature, that is, on his disposition and genius.
What is actual with parents, and confirmed by habit, puts on nature...
They had thought that all things are of nature.
Two things appear essential, because they are proper to nature; space and time. Hence to live in space and time, is to live in the world of nature.
Each and all things in nature represent.
Instead of the Creator of the universe, they think of nature.
That conjugial love is Heaven, is represented in the kingdoms of nature; for there is nothing in universal nature which docs not in some way represent the Lord's Kingdom in general...
Nothing seems to them more wise than to attribute each and all things to nature.
Those who in thought, will not or cannot ascend beyond nature.
There are very many who ascribe... each and all things to nature.
For each and all things in nature are ultimate images...
How gross... is human intelligence which attributes every thing to nature separate... from an influx prior to itself... Angelic wisdom is to attribute nothing to nature.
It is contrary to the affection of falsity... to say that nature continually subsists, as it had [originally] come forth, from the Divine of the Lord.
There are such comparatives in nature, which are also Representatives; for universal nature is a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom...
Hence the Angels know... the most secret things in the world, and in its universal nature.
Man is born into the nature of his parents...
The nature itself which he has contracted in the world by actual life, remains.
This nature is that which is to be extirpated while he lives in the world, which can never be done except by regeneration...

Man has been so created that the Divine things of the Lord might descend through him even to the ultimates of nature, and from the ultimates of nature ascend to Him; so that man might be a medium uniting the Divine with the world of nature; and thus through man... the ultimate itself of nature might live from the Divine...
When they thus contemplated the lower and ultimate things of nature, these appear before their eyes as if they were alive...
In universal nature, each and all things relate to good and truth; for in nature are represented the celestial and spiritual goods and truths which are of Heaven...
Through which ultimate there is apparently as it were an entrance from nature. Signified, Explained.

For it is the natural mind with man through which the things of Heaven... inflow and descend into nature; and through the same mind the things which are of nature ascend. But that it is apparently an entrance from nature through the natural mind into interior things...
The learned more than the simple... ascribe all things to nature...
The inmosts of seeds... are in an interior and more perfect nature.
They knew that universal nature is a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom...
Which they call His human nature.
All who believe in a Supreme Being (merely), worship nature.
Those who attribute all things to nature are among those (who are in fatuous lumen).
This Divine Itself is what is commonly called the Divine nature...

If all things were to be denied the causes of which are not known, innumerable things which come forth in nature would be denied, the causes of which are known scarcely as to the ten-thousandth part... How much more must this be the case with the arcana which come forth in the sphere which is above nature...
The ear is altogether formed to the nature of their modifications...
Whatever secret is hidden in the nature of air and sound... and in the nature of ether and light...

Not only the sensory organs, but also the motory ones, and all the viscera, as to their corporeal and material things, correspond to those things which are in the nature of the world, so that the whole body is an organ composed of the most secret things of all which are in the nature of the world...
(Thus) whatever is in the world and its nature does not come forth from itself, but from what is prior to itself...
Hence... each and all things, even to the ultimates of nature, have not only come forth from the First, but also subsist from the First...

As each and all things which are in the world and its nature come forth, and perpetually come forth... from things prior to themselves, it follows that they come forth and subsist from a World which is above nature... And as there must be a continual connection with that World... it follows that the purer or interior things which are in nature, consequently which are in man, are from thence; and also, that (they) are such forms as can receive the influx.
As in nature there is one only fountain of light and heat...
Every nature which man has put on in the life of the body he retains in the other life; and it is known that the nature cannot be expelled; and that if it is expelled, nothing of life remains.
For they distinguish between the Divine nature and the human nature...
Thinking nothing from doctrine then concerning the distinction between the Divine nature and the human nature.
Most of those (who say that they acknowledge a Supreme Being) acknowledge no God, but in His place nature; they acknowledge nature because they apprehend it...

They were some of those who had been at the Council when it was decreed concerning the Lord's two natures, the Divine and the human... They said that... they had concluded to attribute to the Lord both the Divine and the Human principally because otherwise the papal chair would not subsist. Explained.
For they see that the several things in nature are below man...
In all other things which are of nature he sees confirmations; and at last in universal nature he sees a representative of the heavenly Kingdom.

For nature is that in which are terminated those things which are of the Spiritual World, and which are of Heaven. Hence it is that universal nature is a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom, and that each thing there represents; and that nature subsists from influx according to this order; and that without this influx it could not subsist for a moment.

In these places are those who have ascribed all things to nature, and little to the Divine... When I discoursed with them concerning the Divine Providence, they attributed all things to nature; but still those who have led a good moral life there... successively put off these principles...

Beneath the left foot, a little to the left, are such as have attributed all things to nature, and still have confessed a Being of the universe from Whom are all things of nature... From which it was evident that they had not acknowledged a Creator... but nature.
Those who do what is good from nature, and not from religion. Explained.
They (believe) that nature is all in all.

It is a fallacy of merely natural sense that all things are of nature, and from nature; and that in purer or interior nature there is indeed something which is not apprehended; but if it is said that within or above nature there is what is spiritual and celestial, this is rejected...

When he regards nature from the order of Things, he sees that nature is a complex of means... Whereas a sensuous man does not comprehend that there can be anything distinct from nature, thus neither that there is any Being which is above nature.
The derivations in the lower degrees are only compositions... with such things added from purer nature, and afterwards from grosser, as can serve as containing vessels...

This cannot possibly be believed by those who attribute all things to nature, and nothing to the Divine; whereas those who attribute all things to the Divine, and nothing to nature, are given to see that every single thing is from (the influx of the Spiritual World)... and also that (it) corresponds... and finally it is given them to see that universal nature is a theatre representative of the Lord's Kingdom; thus that the Divine is in every single thing. Explained.
Each and all things in nature succeed each other as end, cause, and effect...
Yet the case is that in each and all things in nature and its three kingdoms there is inwardly ai agent from the Spiritual World...
Thence come forth very many things which the man who attributes all things to nature either denies or attributes to more occult nature. Example(s).
Such an image of marriage is in each and all things of nature, and of its three kingdoms. For in order that anything may come forth in nature, there must be heat and light...
(The things of faith and charity can be applied to) all the truths of interior and exterior nature, both visible and invisible, because these correspond to spiritual truths.
As each and all things in nature... relate to good and truth...
Time and space are proper to nature.
He then from sensuous things forms some truths which... still remain within those things which are in nature.
They were from the Hells where are those who... have deduced all things to nature. Described.
They thence derive a nature which remains after death.

Those who have believed that nature is everything, and have confirmed themselves in this, and have thence lived a secure life... when they appear in the light of Heaven, do not appear to have any face, but in place of it something bearded...
There are at this day very many in the Christian world who ascribe all things to nature... but more in one nation than in another.
The things in nature are nothing but effects...
The eye does not see even the more prominent things which are in ultimate nature... How then could it see the things which are within even the purer nature?
Attributing all things to nature... thus have they closed the interiors...
All the secrets of interior nature are inscribed and applied to (the body)... (so) that universal nature conduces to form the external of man...
There are men who... are corporeal, being those who... have ascribed all things to nature. Described.
Can be illustrated by very many things in nature.
Those in truth and not yet in good, reason... from fallacies from lowest nature. Signified, Explained.
The worshippers of nature especially can never be induced to believe that...

Then in place of (the idea of a universal Being) there comes the idea of nature, to which each and all things are attributed. Thence is the worship of nature so common at this day, especially in the Christian world.
Deep beneath them are those who... have worshipped nature...
(Thus) there are continual successions from the First... even to the ultimates which are in nature...
Everything which is not attributed to nature is (now) denied.
If the man of the Church were to see the veriest Divine miracles, he would first deduce them into nature...
He reasons from mere falsities who attributes all things to nature... when yet all things are from the Divine, and nature is only the instrumental.
All evil which by habit has contracted as it were nature is derived into the offspring.
Each and all things in universal nature come forth from interior things in order: they are derivations and successions...
To these the sciences are means of... confirming for nature against the Divine...
Or he takes up an idea of the Divine... which conjoins itself with the idea of the worshippers of nature; and thus becomes null.
Except those who... ascribe all things to nature.
In this way they act from their nature itself acquired in the world...
The second religiosity is that in which the lumen of nature is everything. Explained... Some of these... place the Divine in nature; for their lumen, being of nature, falls into nature...
It is believed... that man from the lumen of nature... can know many things which are of religion...

The learned... who have raised the lumen of their nature above that of others... more than others... for the Divine acknowledge nature... Hence it is evident what is the reality of the lumen of nature without revelation.
Evils confirmed imbue nature, so that afterwards they can scarcely be extirpated. Explained.

elements.injection1: that is, the heavens with the sun, moon, stars, and the Earth with the subjects of its three kingdoms

elements.str: Those who do not believe in one God under a human form... their thought effuses itself into the universe without determination, and thus falls into nature, which they thus acknowledge in place of God.
For each and all things in nature relate to the human form...
For all the representatives in nature relate to the human form...

Hence he observes that all things in nature relate to such things as are in the Spiritual World; and he who can conclude further, perceives that nature does not subsist from itself, but through influx from Heaven...
For the ultimate of Divine order is in the nature of the world.
The things which appear in nature, in its three kingdoms, are the ultimates of Divine order; for all things of Heaven are terminated in them...
His idea of the invisible God was no other than as of nature in its primes; from which it resulted that the inmost of nature was to him His Divine.
For he who thinks from nature and its lumen alone...
Do not such see nature for God; some that nature which is before the eyes; some that nature which is not before the eyes?
The Angels are astounded when they hear that there are men who attribute all things to nature...
Nature has been created only to invest what is spiritual, and present it correspondent in the ultimate of order.
Hence all things... in the nature of the world which are in Divine order relate to good and truth.
In the nature of the world, in its three kingdoms, all things which come forth there according to order are forms of uses, or effects formed by use for use; and therefore (they) are correspondences.
For nature begins from this sun... But the Spiritual... is above nature... and they communicate solely by correspondences.
The learned... who had ascribed all things to nature were found to have their interiors completely closed...
For they who acknowledge nature for the Divine all think from the corporeal Sensuous...
Those who have ascribed all things to nature... in the other life study magical arts...
Those who have... regarded nature as relatively dead, and merely subservient to spiritual things, and have confirmed themselves in this, are in heavenly light. Described.
The will is the very nature or native quality of man...
The evils (of good Spirits) have been of a different kind or nature...
In these Hells are all those who have acknowledged nature, and denied the Divine...
The reason (many of the intelligent do not believe in immortality) is that at heart they... for the Divine acknowledge nature. Explained.
Hence the Lord had... a Divine essence from the Father, and a human nature from the mother... This human nature from the mother He did not transmute into the Divine Essence...
To think about God from space is to think about the extense of nature.
How sensuously... those think who say that nature is from itself.
Nor can it be seen that all things of nature are from (love and wisdom), unless nature is regarded from uses in their series and in their order...
Therefore if forms alone are regarded, not anything of life can be seen in nature, still less anything of love and wisdom; thus not anything of God.

Hence it is that man can he elevated above nature, differently from any animal; can think analytically and rationally concerning the civil and moral things which are within nature, and also concerning the spiritual and celestial things which are above nature.
There are two things proper to nature: space and time...
But if he denies the Divine omnipresence, and ascribes all things to nature, he does not want to be elevated...
For not anything proper to nature can be predicated of the Divine...
Nature derives this measurement from the apparent gyration... of the sun.

His delirium is caused by [the idea] that God has come forth from Himself, from which he falls downwards into the origin of nature from itself; from which idea be cannot be set loose except by the spiritual... idea concerning eternity...
The Angels say that... in no way can they perceive nature from eternity; still less nature from itself; and not at all nature as nature in itself...

When man dies, he steps entirely out of the world of nature, and leaves behind all things of it, and enters into a World in which there is nothing of nature; and in that World he lives so separated from nature that there is not any communication by continuity...

For man... has not penetrated deeper than into the interior or purer things of nature; and therefore many have feigned the habitations of the Angels... in the ether, and some in the stars; thus within nature, and not above or outside of it; when yet Angels and Spirits are entirely above or outside of nature...
That... nature, because it derives its origin from this sun, is dead. General article.
That nature appears in man and animal as alive, is from the life which accompanies and actuates.

From these things can be seen the fatuity of those who ascribe all things to nature. Those who have confirmed themselves from nature have induced on themselves the state that they no longer want to elevate the mind above nature; and therefore their minds are closed above, and open below. Described.

No one but a person bereaved of reason can think that all things are from nature, and that even life is from it... Nature cannot dispose life to anything, for nature in itself is altogether inert. Explained.
The Lord could not enter into (the third degree) except by a nature like human nature... For thus He could put off nature, which in itself is dead, and yet is a receptacle of the Divine...
He then acknowledges nature as the creatress of the universe.
Fearing that thus they should (think) that... nature is from itself, and thus that the inmost of it is what is called God.
As the Divine is not in space, it is not continuous, as is the inmost of nature.

This is why those who have written on the origin of plants and animals could not do otherwise than deduce it from nature; and if from God, that God from the beginning implanted in nature the force of producing such things: thus not knowing that no force has been implanted in nature; for in itself it is dead, and no more contributes to produce these things than as an instrument does in the work of a workman, which in order to act must be perpetually moved. It is the Spiritual which... proceeds to the ultimates of nature, that produces the forms of plants and animals...

Sir Hans Sloane... ascribed these things to nature, [saying] that the power and force for producing such things has been implanted in it from creation... Martin Folkes said that that force is continuous from God the Creator in nature... Sir Hans Sloane was convinced by this experience that nature contributes nothing whatever to the productions of plants and animals... He added... that if he had known the things he now knows of the Spiritual World, he would have ascribed to nature no more than that it subserves the Spiritual which is from God for fixing those things which continually inflow into nature.
That the visible things... testify that nature has produced nothing, and does produce nothing... General article.

Those who confirm... that the sun... produces the things... upon the Earth, at last ascribe all things to nature... These can afterwards say that God has created nature, and has implanted in it the power of producing such things; but... by God the Creator they mean nature; some its inmost...
Some are to be excused in that they have ascribed some visible things to nature. Explained.
These are two reasons for excusing those who have believed that nature produces the visible things from what was implanted from creation.
But those who by confirmations in favour of nature have made atheists of themselves, are not to be excused, because they could have confirmed themselves in favour of the Divine...
Therefore the same who have confirmed themselves in favour of nature even to the separation of the Divine from it, do not account anything as sin...

Those who believe in the Divine operation in each thing of nature can confirm themselves in favour of the Divine by very many things which they see in nature, more than those who confirm themselves in favour of nature. Explained.
Those who ascribe all things to nature do indeed see such things, but only think that they exist

; and they say that nature produces them; and this they say because they have averted their minds from thinking about the Divine; and those who have (done this), when they see the wonderful things in nature, cannot think rationally, still less spiritually... and then they think in nature from nature, and not above nature, in like manner as do those who are in Hell...
Those who have confirmed themselves in favour of nature... have been seen by me in the Spiritual World. Described.
Therefore let everyone beware of confirmations in favour of nature...
Such a one is in everything not seen with the eye, whether it is in interior nature, or in the Spiritual World.
(Thus) there can be no thought about nature from eternity; (nor) about creation from nature; for space and time are proper to nature.
Nor are freedom itself and rationality itself possible with those who attribute all things to nature...

It must be thought, either that God rules all things, or that nature does... He who thinks that nature rules all things, thinks that natural heat and light do so, which, however, are in themselves dead...
This desire lies inmostly hidden... in the nature of man's life.
They attribute (the Divine Providence) either to man or to nature... Explained.
If they should see as in clear day that nature in itself is dead... still those who have confirmed themselves in favour of nature would not (acknowledge the Divine Providence).
From constant and stated things... some find arguments for their delirium in favour of nature...
Those who ascribe all things to nature also ascribe all things to human prudence; for those who ascribe all things to nature, at heart deny God...

It is the like with the name of a universal Providence... when it is said concerning nature, and it is meant that God created the universe, and implanted in nature that it should produce all things from itself...
But the Thing in itself is... that the Divine Providence is in the most singular things of nature... and, from these, is universal.
That those who have acknowledged nature alone... make Hell. Explained.
All who lead an evil life, interiorly acknowledge nature alone... Explained.
(This) is from man's proprium, which is his nature, and is called his soul from his parent.
The acknowledgement of nature alone is hidden in every evil. Explained.
They reason in favour of nature, and against God...
Those who acknowledge nature... are as the Spirits of Hell. Described.
Who does not speak... in favour of nature, when he speaks from the external man?
Write books... one in favour of nature...
Man first puts on the grosser things of nature... but by death he puts these off, and retains the purer things of nature, which are nearest to spiritual things; and these are then his containants.
As the extremes and ultimates of nature cannot receive the spiritual and eternal things for which the human mind has been formed, as these are in themselves... man puts them off...

(The love of self) can confirm by a thousand arguments that nature has created itself; and that it afterwards created men, beasts, and plants of every kind; and also that by influx from its interior self it causes men to live, to think analytically, and to understand wisely.
The insanities which nature itself, which in itself is dead, inspires into his phantasy.
